attachments.text:
As a marketing & growth leader, grinding every day, I’ve never felt this far behind. AI is moving at a frightening pace.

You could say, ever since ChatGPT launched, I’ve dived headfirst into AI.

- My full-time role is AI-centric
- I co-host a YouTube channel on AI
- I write a Substack on AI
- I do talks on AI
- I do advisory on AI & GTM
- I invest in pre-seed / seed stage AI companies
- My WhatsApp is filled with conversations about AI with v.smart people
- In ChatGPT’s 2025 year-in-review, they ranked my usage in the top 0.1% of users

I’m in pretty deep. But I feel so behind.

Not behind the ‘competition’. There’s no doubt I know a lot about AI, but many people know a lot more than me, and I’m thankful I get to spend time with many of them. But that’s not why I feel behind.

I feel behind the opportunity. There’s so much opportunity right now. I have so much I want to learn and build.

It’s jarring. I spent my holiday break bookmarking dozens of incredible threads about Claude Code. There are several apps I’m in the midst of building or planning to build. I have a whole To Do list with agents to build. I should know more ways to use Notebook LLM; it’s awesome. I should have more Claude Skills built. I’ve done 20 hours on VEO3.1 in the past couple of weeks, but I should know more. I’m not spending enough time with Opus 4.5 / Gemini 3 / Replits autonomous agent, and on and on and on.

It’s a lot.

When there’s an abundance of opportunity, everything looks tempting.

What I tell myself is - FOCUS. Master a couple of things at a time. It’s better to be great at a couple of things than average at many.

Hopefully, this stream of thoughts is helpful to others who feel the same.

2026 → Focus, Grind, Be Curious, Ship | 120 comments on LinkedIn

je pense qu'il faut pas t'attendre à des trucs de dingues non plus (et je sais ce que j'ai mis dans ma candidature pour le coup :)).
Je freine un peu sur l'IA en ce moment, parce que le temps passé à tester plein de trucs vaut pas encore l'investissement et j'ai un vrai travail quand meme.
• J'ai mes trucs de base (chatgpt pour les brainstormings, claude pour la recherche, notebooklm pour pas me farcir des tonnes de trucs à lire, gamma/nano banana pour les decks, granola pour les calls). Et basta pour l'orga perso, je passe surement à côté de plein de trucs, mais j'attends que les use cases murissent un peu.
• Je laisse les équipes lancer tout ce dont ils ont besoin, du coup on a plein de process batards avec de l'humain et du llm, osef que ça ressemble à rien tant que ça marche.
